title: Integrating MySQL with Web APIs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Integrating MySQL with Web APIs”?
options: An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.
It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.
questions.answer_key: An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Integrating MySQL with Web APIs” safely?
options: Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Write a parameterized query using the target driver, keep credentials in environment configuration, and specify error/cleanup behavior.
questions.answer_key: Write a parameterized query using the target driver, keep credentials in environment configuration, and specify error/cleanup behavior.
questions.explanation: Write a parameterized query using the target driver, keep credentials in environment configuration, and specify error/cleanup behavior. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Integrating MySQL with Web APIs”, what should be verified?
options: Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
